points.en: Vehicle-trauma prevention bundle: correct use of age-appropriate infant/child car seats, occupant restraints paired with functioning air bags, community pedestrian-safety education, motorcycle helmet use, and eliminating distracted or impaired driving.
points.zh: 机动车创伤预防清单：正确使用的婴儿/儿童安全座椅、安全带和气囊、行人安全项目、摩托车头盔，还有杜绝分心和醉驾。

points.en: Cycling and recreation prevention bundle: bicycle helmets, bike paths separated from vehicle traffic, appropriate safety padding and apparel for skating and skateboarding, and soft energy-absorbent playground surfaces.
points.zh: 骑行与娱乐预防清单：自行车头盔、与车道分离的自行车道、滑冰滑板的护具和装备、操场用能吸能的软质地面。

points.en: Drowning-prevention bundle: four-sided locked pool enclosures plus pool alarms, immediate adult supervision, caregiver CPR training, swim lessons, pool/beach safety instruction, and personal flotation devices.
points.zh: 溺水预防清单：四面带锁的泳池围栏加泳池报警器、大人全程在场监护、照护者学 CPR、游泳课、泳池/海滩安全教育、个人救生衣。

points.en: Poisoning, burns, and other prevention bundle: safe storage of chemicals/meds with child-safety packaging; well-maintained electrical appliances/cords plus smoke and carbon-monoxide detectors and safe stovetop cookware placement; and discouraging infant walkers, gating stairways, and first-aid training for babysitters and childcare workers.
points.zh: 中毒、烧伤及其他预防清单：化学品药物安全存放加儿童安全包装；电器电线定期维护、装烟雾/一氧化碳报警器、炉具摆放讲究；不鼓励用学步车、楼梯口装安全门、给保姆和托育人员做急救培训。

points.en: Clinical mindset reminder: in a seriously injured child, assume every organ system is hurt until proven otherwise — don't let the obvious injury make you stop looking.
points.zh: 临床心态提醒：重伤儿童要假设全身每个器官系统都可能受伤，直到证明没事——别让明显的那处伤让你停止继续找。

points.en: Applied numbers from the case wrap-up: for a 2-year-old, minimum acceptable SBP = 70 + (2 x 2) = 74 mmHg; once the ABCs are addressed in a shocked child, don't burn time hunting for a hard peripheral IV — go IO early, then bolus 20 mL/kg.
points.zh: 案例复盘里的数字应用：2 岁孩子的最低可接受收缩压 = 70 + (2 x 2) = 74 mmHg；休克患儿一旦 ABC 处理完，别死磕难打的外周静脉——尽早上骨内通路，然后推等张液 20 mL/kg。

atScene.en: Build your general impression with the PAT from the doorway, hands off, before anything touches the child.
atScene.zh: 站在门口用 PAT 完成总体印象，先不动手，任何东西都别先碰到孩子。

atScene.en: Mark where mottling or pallor ends on the limbs; if the line creeps toward the trunk on recheck, the shell-to-core shunt — and the shock — is getting worse.
atScene.zh: 记下四肢花斑或苍白的分界线在哪；复评时分界线往躯干爬，说明外周向核心的血流重分配在加重——休克在恶化。

atScene.en: Read pulse oximetry in context: cold or poorly perfused fingers lie. Always match the waveform against the palpated pulse and ECG rate.
atScene.zh: 血氧要放进情境里读：手指冰凉、灌注差时读数会骗人。永远把波形和摸到的脉搏、ECG 心率对上号再信。

atScene.en: Blood pressure is only one data point — decide stability from the whole PAT, exam, and vitals, because compensated shock coexists with a normal pressure.
atScene.zh: 血压只是一个数据点——稳定与否要靠 PAT、查体和整套生命体征一起定，代偿性休克完全可以顶着正常血压存在。

atScene.en: Treat pain as a pediatric vital sign: assess it, treat it, and reassess it with every set of vitals.
atScene.zh: 把疼痛当儿科生命体征：评估、处理，然后随每一轮生命体征复评。

atScene.en: For croup or bronchiolitis, try gentle nasal suctioning before reaching for a drug — clearing an obligate nose-breather's nares can resolve distress on its own.
atScene.zh: 遇到 croup 或毛细支气管炎，先试轻柔吸鼻再想着用药——只用鼻呼吸的孩子，光是清通鼻腔就可能自己缓解。

atScene.en: Never open a suspected epiglottitis child's mouth to look, and never delay for an IV — either can flip a partial obstruction into a complete one within minutes.
atScene.zh: 怀疑会厌炎绝不能张口看咽部，也别为了扎针拖时间——两者都可能在几分钟内把部分梗阻变成完全梗阻。

atScene.en: Cap every intubation attempt at 20 seconds by the clock, not by feel — reoxygenate with bag-mask before trying again rather than pushing for one more try.
atScene.zh: 每次插管尝试要按秒表卡在 20 秒，不是凭感觉——宁可退回球囊面罩重新给氧再试，也别硬撑多插一下。

atScene.en: In decompensated shock, don't burn scene time chasing a vein — one IV attempt, then straight to IO and start fluid therapy.
atScene.zh: 失代偿性休克别在找血管上耗现场时间——静脉只试一次，不成功立刻改骨髓腔通路，开始补液。

atScene.en: Warn caregivers before pressing an ice-filled glove to an infant's whole face for a vagal manoeuvre — done without warning, it looks like you're hurting the child.
atScene.zh: 用装冰水的手套敷住婴儿整张脸做迷走神经手法前，先提醒照护者——没打招呼直接做，看着像是在虐待孩子。

atScene.en: In suspected cardiogenic shock, give a single fluid bolus slowly and watch closely — worsening work of breathing, falling SpO2, or worsening perfusion after that bolus confirms the diagnosis and is your signal to stop giving fluid.
atScene.zh: 怀疑心源性休克时，缓慢给一次单剂补液并密切观察——如果补液后呼吸做功加重、SpO2 下降或灌注变差，就证实了诊断，也是该停止补液的信号。

atScene.en: Always check the glucose level for a patient with altered mental status — regardless of what else the history suggests.
atScene.zh: 任何意识改变的患者都必须查血糖——不管病史看起来多么指向别的病因。

atScene.en: Gown up before you touch a child with possible meningitis: gown, gloves, mask, and eye shield for yourself, and a mask on the patient too — meningococcus spreads easily by droplet.
atScene.zh: 接触疑似脑膜炎的孩子前先做好防护：自己穿隔离衣、戴手套口罩护目面屏，也给患者戴上口罩——脑膜炎球菌很容易经飞沫传播。

atScene.en: Always collect pill bottles or chemical containers from the scene and transport them with the patient — they can be the fastest way for the ED to identify the agent and dose.
atScene.zh: 现场的药瓶或化学品容器一定要收集起来随患者带走——这往往是急诊室最快确认毒物种类和剂量的方式。

atScene.en: Only dilute an ingestion with milk or water after checking with Poison Control or medical control, and never if there's any airway or breathing concern.
atScene.zh: 用牛奶或水稀释口服毒物前，先联系中毒控制中心或医疗指导；只要有任何气道或呼吸方面的顾虑，就不要给喝。

atScene.en: At a possible SIDS scene, weigh recent illness, chronic conditions, medications, or trauma history against crib clues like pillows, stuffed toys, blind cords, or sheepskin — the latter push suffocation up the differential even amid the family's shock.
atScene.zh: 疑似 SIDS 现场，把近期患病、慢病、用药、外伤史和床里的枕头、毛绒玩具、百叶窗拉绳、羊皮垫这些线索放在一起权衡——后者会把窒息往前排，哪怕全家都乱作一团。

atScene.en: At a BRUE scene the baby usually looks fine again by the time you arrive — resist the urge to downplay it. Give life support only if there's real cardiorespiratory compromise or altered mental status, but transport every BRUE history regardless of how good the baby looks now.
atScene.zh: BRUE 现场，你到的时候宝宝往往已经恢复正常——别因此就轻描淡写。真有心肺损害或意识改变才做生命支持，但只要有 BRUE 病史，不管宝宝现在看起来多好都要转运。

atScene.en: At a suspected-maltreatment scene, write down what you literally see and hear — home condition, caregiver-child interaction, and any concerning quote in quotation marks with who said it and when — and save your concerns for the receiving hospital, never for the caregiver's face.
atScene.zh: 疑似虐待现场，把亲眼所见亲耳所听照实记下——居家状况、照护者和孩子的互动、可疑的话原话加引号并注明是谁、什么时候说的——疑虑留给接收医院，绝不当面甩给照护者。

atScene.en: On a pediatric trauma scene, an ominous mechanism earns load-and-go treatment no matter how good the child looks right now — a compensated shock picture can hide behind a steady blood pressure and a fast heart rate for a surprisingly long time.
atScene.zh: 儿科创伤现场，机制凶险就该按 load-and-go 处理，不管孩子现在看起来多稳——代偿性休克能靠一个稳住的血压和一个偏快的心率藏很久。

atScene.en: At a burn scene, use the rule of palms — the child's own palm without fingers equals 1% BSA — to size up scattered or patchy burns fast, and read the pattern itself: irregular edges fit an accidental splash, sharp demarcation lines or a buttocks burn do not.
atScene.zh: 烧伤现场用手掌法快速估算——孩子自己的手掌（不含手指）等于1% 体表面积——散在、不规则的烧伤这样估最快；再看伤型本身：边缘不规则符合意外泼溅，边界清晰或臀部烫伤则不太对劲。

atScene.en: At a technology-assisted child's home, the caregiver is your fastest diagnostic tool and usually has a spare tracheostomy tube on hand — lean on their expertise for what's normal for this specific child before you start troubleshooting equipment on your own.
atScene.zh: 技术依赖儿童的家里，照护者是你最快的诊断工具，手边通常就有备用气切管——先问清楚"这个孩子平时正常是什么样"，再自己动手排查设备。

atScene.en: On a behavioural-emergency call, scan for weapons and flight risk before you scan for a diagnosis, and position your crew so a bolt-prone child can't slip past you while you're still building rapport.
atScene.zh: 行为急症现场，先查有没有武器、孩子会不会跑，再谈诊断；建立信任的同时把队员站位摆好，别让容易出逃的孩子从你身边溜走。

atScene.en: Every pediatric call is a prevention opportunity — noting the injury mechanism (unfenced pool, unhelmeted rider, unsecured car seat) and flagging it to family or community programs is as much a part of the job as the run itself.
atScene.zh: 每次儿科出车都是一次预防机会——记下伤害机制（没围栏的泳池、没戴头盔、没固定好的安全座椅）并反馈给家庭或社区项目，和救治本身一样是工作的一部分。

confusions.en: A respiratory rate that drifts back to normal in a child who has been labouring is not improvement — it is fatigue announcing imminent failure. Trust the trend plus work of breathing, never a single reassuring number.
confusions.zh: 费力呼吸的孩子频率「回落到正常」不是好转，是累到快撑不住的前奏。要信趋势加呼吸做功，不要信单独一个好看的数字。

confusions.en: Normal SpO2 does not rule out respiratory distress: the child may be spending enormous effort to hold that saturation. The PAT catches what the oximeter misses.
confusions.zh: 血氧正常不等于没有呼吸窘迫：那可能是孩子用全部力气换来的数字。PAT 能抓住血氧仪漏掉的东西。

confusions.en: Acrocyanosis — blue hands and feet in an infant under 2 months — is a normal response to cold; true cyanosis involves skin and mucous membranes and is a late sign of cardiorespiratory failure.
confusions.zh: 肢端发绀——2 个月以下婴儿手脚发蓝——是受凉的正常反应；真发绀累及皮肤加黏膜，而且是心肺衰竭的晚期信号。

confusions.en: Grunting sounds like whimpering but is a hypoxia alarm; conversely, a strong loud cry is reassuring. Do not let volume fool you in either direction.
confusions.zh: 呻吟音听着像小声哼唧，其实是缺氧警报；反过来，响亮有力的大哭反而让人放心。别在任何一个方向上被音量骗了。

confusions.en: An interactive, normotensive child can still be in compensated shock — pallor and tachycardia may be the only clues. Waiting for hypotension means waiting for decompensation.
confusions.zh: 还能互动、血压正常的孩子照样可能处于代偿性休克——线索可能只有苍白和心动过速。等到低血压才行动，等来的就是失代偿。

confusions.en: Harsh sounds heard in the chest may be transmitted from the upper airway. If unsure, listen over the nose or trachea to separate stridor and congestion from true lung sounds.
confusions.zh: 胸部听到的粗糙音可能是上气道传导下来的。拿不准时把听诊器放到鼻部或气管上对比，把喘鸣、鼻塞音和真正的肺部啰音分开。

confusions.en: A quieting wheeze in a struggling asthmatic sounds like relief, but paired with reduced air movement it means severe obstruction and fatigue, not improvement — the same trap as a normalizing respiratory rate.
confusions.zh: 费力挣扎的哮喘患儿哮鸣声变小听着像好转，但如果同时进气量也在减少，那是重度梗阻加力竭，不是变好——和呼吸频率「回归正常」是同一个陷阱。

confusions.en: FBAO management skips the usual systematic approach: once the patient collapses, go straight to compressions with no pulse check, unlike almost every other pediatric emergency where you assess before you act.
confusions.zh: 异物梗阻的处理跳过平时的系统流程：孩子一旦倒地就直接按压，不判脉——这和几乎所有其他儿科急症「先评估再动手」的套路不一样。

confusions.en: Warm, flushed skin with bounding pulses in early distributive (septic) shock looks reassuring compared with pale, mottled hypovolemic shock — it is not; it's the early phase of the same downward trajectory, just before it converges on the classic hypoperfused picture.
confusions.zh: 分布性（脓毒性）休克早期皮肤温暖发红、脉搏有力，比起苍白花斑的低血容量性休克看着让人安心——其实不是；那只是同一条下坡路的早期阶段，晚一点表现就会和典型的低灌注画面趋同。

confusions.en: Sinus tachycardia and SVT can both present as a fast, narrow-complex rhythm in an irritable, vomiting infant — the differentiator is rate stability and range: sinus tachycardia varies with stimulus, while SVT sits fixed above 220 (infant) or 180 (child) beats/min with absent or abnormal P waves.
confusions.zh: 窦性心动过速和 SVT 在一个烦躁呕吐的婴儿身上都能表现为窄 QRS 心动过速——区分点在心率是否稳定、区间在哪：窦性心动过速会随刺激变化，SVT 则固定在婴儿 >220 或儿童 >180 次/分，且 P 波消失或异常。

confusions.en: The height of a fever does not predict how sick the child actually is — a mildly febrile young infant can be harbouring serious bacterial illness, while a toddler burning at 40°C from a common viral bug can look and act relatively fine once the fever is treated.
confusions.zh: 发热的高低不能预测孩子病得有多重——低烧的小婴儿可能正藏着严重细菌感染，而普通病毒感染烧到 40°C 的幼儿，退了烧可能精神状态相对还不错。

confusions.en: A young child with suspected meningitis often has no nuchal rigidity at all — that classic sign is unreliable below school age. Don't wait for a stiff neck before you suspect meningitis in an infant; fever plus lethargy, poor feeding, or a bulging fontanelle is enough.
confusions.zh: 怀疑脑膜炎的小孩子常常根本没有颈项强直——这个典型体征在学龄前很不可靠。别等脖子发硬才怀疑婴儿得了脑膜炎；发热加嗜睡、喂养差或囟门膨隆就该起疑了。

confusions.en: A toddler who ingested "just one pill" is not automatically low-risk — some single tablets (clonidine, propranolol, verapamil, theophylline) are dosed for adult bodies and can be lethal in a small child.
confusions.zh: 幼儿「只吃了一颗药」不代表风险就低——有些单片药（可乐定、普萘洛尔、维拉帕米、茶碱）本来是按成人体重设计的剂量，对小孩子可能致命。

confusions.en: Syrup of ipecac is a leftover home-remedy habit, not current practice — it doesn't remove meaningful toxin and should never be used or recommended in prehospital pediatric poisoning management.
confusions.zh: 吐根糖浆是过时的家庭习惯做法，不是现行做法——它去除不了多少毒物，院前儿科中毒处理绝不应该使用或建议使用。

confusions.en: Myth: BRUE is a 'near-miss SIDS.' Reality: the two labels have been dropped — BRUE and SIDS just share an age window, they are not points on the same disease spectrum, and one does not predict the other.
confusions.zh: 误区：BRUE 是"未遂 SIDS"。事实：这两个旧说法都已废弃——BRUE 和 SIDS 只是年龄段重叠，并不在同一疾病谱上，二者互不预示。

confusions.en: Myth: any bluish 'bruise' on the lower back/buttocks or dramatic circular skin marks mean abuse. Reality: Mongolian spots are a normal birthmark, and coining/cupping are harmless traditional fever remedies — neither is maltreatment.
confusions.zh: 误区：腰骶臀部的青蓝色"瘀伤"或吓人的圆形皮痕就是虐待。事实：蒙古斑是正常胎记，刮痧拔罐是无害的民间退热法——都不算虐待。

confusions.en: Myth: real abuse always leaves visible marks. Reality: shaken baby syndrome typically shows a grossly abnormal-looking child with zero external injury signs — the tell is a history that can't explain the clinical picture, not bruising.
confusions.zh: 误区：真虐待一定留下看得见的痕迹。事实：摇晃婴儿综合征往往外观极差却毫无外伤征象——真正的破绽是病史解释不了临床表现，不是瘀伤。

confusions.en: Myth: a normal blood pressure rules out significant blood loss in a child. Reality: pediatric vasoconstriction is so effective that BP can hold steady deep into hemorrhagic shock — tachycardia with a concerning mechanism is the earlier, more reliable red flag.
confusions.zh: 误区：血压正常就代表没大出血。事实：孩子的血管收缩代偿能力极强，出血性休克进展很深血压还能撑住——机制可疑加心动过速才是更早、更靠谱的红旗。

confusions.en: Myth: any burn over 5% BSA automatically triggers BC's formal IV fluid protocol. Reality: the textbook's 5% is a general prehospital fluid-resuscitation guideline, while BC's hypovolemia protocol indication is specifically burns >20% BSA (partial and full thickness) — know both, but chart to BC's line.
confusions.zh: 误区：烧伤只要超过 5% BSA 就自动进入 BC 正式静脉补液协议。事实：教材的 5% 是通用院前补液指引，BC 低血容量协议的正式指征是烧伤 >20% BSA（部分层+全层）——两条都要懂，但落地按 BC 的线走。

confusions.en: Myth: any problem with a G-tube, central line, or shunt is an EMS emergency requiring aggressive field intervention. Reality: most G-tube issues need only supportive care and transport, and even a working central line is a last-resort access point, not a first move — reserve urgency for real red flags like a pulled G-tube, line infection, or shunt obstruction/infection.
confusions.zh: 误区：G 管、中心静脉导管或分流管一出问题就是要现场大动干戈的急症。事实：多数 G 管问题支持治疗加转运就够；就算中心静脉导管在正常工作也只是最后手段而非首选——真正该紧张的是 G 管整根脱出、导管感染、分流管堵塞/感染这类实打实的红旗。

confusions.en: Myth: a violently out-of-control child should get sedating drugs on scene to make transport manageable. Reality: the textbook steers away from chemical restraint in the field when possible — mechanical restraint, carefully documented, is the preferred route.
confusions.zh: 误区：孩子彻底失控就该现场给镇静药方便转运。事实：教材倾向院前尽量避免化学约束——首选是有据可查的机械约束。

mnemonics.name: PAT
mnemonics.en: Pediatric Assessment Triangle: Appearance, Work of breathing, Circulation to skin — the hands-off doorway impression.
mnemonics.zh: 儿科评估三角：外观、呼吸做功、皮肤循环——站在门口不动手完成的总体印象。

mnemonics.name: TICLS
mnemonics.en: Appearance checklist: Tone, Interactiveness, Consolability, Look/gaze, Speech/cry.
mnemonics.zh: 外观五要素：肌张力、互动性、可安抚性、眼神注视、说话/哭声。

mnemonics.name: Pediatric SAMPLE extras
mnemonics.en: Standard SAMPLE plus immunizations, birth history (infants/toddlers), last feed including breast or bottle, and fever history.
mnemonics.zh: 儿科版 SAMPLE 在标准六项外加问：疫苗接种、出生史（婴幼儿）、最后一次进食（含母乳/奶瓶）、发热史。

mnemonics.name: DOPE
mnemonics.en: Deterioration after intubation: Displacement, Obstruction, Pneumothorax, Equipment failure.
mnemonics.zh: 插管后突然恶化排查：Displacement 移位、Obstruction 阻塞、Pneumothorax 气胸、Equipment failure 设备故障。

mnemonics.name: AEIOU-TIPS
mnemonics.en: Differential for altered level of consciousness: Alcohol/acidosis, Epilepsy, Insulin, Overdose, Uremia, Trauma, Infection, Psychosis, Stroke.
mnemonics.zh: 意识改变鉴别诊断：酒精/酸中毒、癫痫、胰岛素、药物过量、尿毒症、外伤、感染、精神疾病、卒中。

mnemonics.name: CHILD ABUSE
mnemonics.en: Screen for suspected maltreatment: C-onsistency of the injury with the child's developmental age; H-istory inconsistent with the injury; I-nappropriate parental concern; L-ack of supervision; D-elay in seeking care; A-ffect of parent/caregiver and child; B-ruises of varying ages; U-nusual injury pattern; S-uspicious circumstances; E-nvironmental clues.
mnemonics.zh: 筛查可疑虐待：C 伤情是否符合孩子的发育年龄；H 病史和伤情对不上；I 家长/照护者反应不合常理；L 缺乏看护；D 延迟就医；A 照护者与孩子的情感表现异常；B 新旧不一的多处瘀伤；U 不寻常的伤型（如皮带扣印、电线印）；S 可疑情境；E 环境线索。

selfCheck.qEn: Name the three arms of the PAT and the five letters of TICLS.
selfCheck.qZh: 说出 PAT 的三条边和 TICLS 五个字母各代表什么。
selfCheck.aEn: PAT: appearance, work of breathing, circulation to skin. TICLS: tone, interactiveness, consolability, look or gaze, speech or cry.
selfCheck.aZh: PAT：外观、呼吸做功、皮肤循环。TICLS：肌张力、互动性、可安抚性、眼神注视、说话或哭声。

selfCheck.qEn: A 4-year-old has a systolic BP of 76 mm Hg. Interpret it.
selfCheck.qZh: 4 岁孩子收缩压 76 mmHg，怎么判？
selfCheck.aEn: Minimum acceptable SBP = 70 + (2 x 4) = 78. At 76 the child is below the floor: decompensated shock.
selfCheck.aZh: 最低可接受收缩压 = 70 + (2 × 4) = 78。76 已经低于底线：失代偿性休克。

selfCheck.qEn: A responsive 8-month-old has a completely obstructed airway. What is the technique, and what changes if the infant goes unresponsive?
selfCheck.qZh: 清醒的 8 个月大婴儿完全气道梗阻，手法是什么？如果婴儿变得无反应又该怎么变？
selfCheck.aEn: Alternate 5 back slaps with 5 chest thrusts while responsive. If unresponsive, skip the pulse check and start chest compressions (30:2 one rescuer), checking the mouth before each ventilation attempt and never doing a blind finger sweep.
selfCheck.aZh: 清醒时 5 次背部叩击和 5 次胸部按压交替。一旦无反应，跳过判脉直接胸外按压（单人 30:2），每次给人工呼吸前先看一眼口腔，绝不做盲探式手指清扫。

selfCheck.qEn: A wheezing asthmatic who called 911 suddenly sounds quieter on auscultation with less audible wheeze. What does this mean, and what is the BC epinephrine dose ceiling if IM epinephrine is indicated?
selfCheck.qZh: 叫了救护车的哮喘患儿听诊突然安静下来、哮鸣音变少了，这意味着什么？如果指征上要打肌注肾上腺素，BC 的剂量上限是多少？
selfCheck.aEn: Decreased air movement with absent wheezing signals severe obstruction and respiratory fatigue, not improvement — treat as impending respiratory arrest. BC epinephrine: 0.01 mg/kg IM to a maximum of 0.5 mg, may repeat up to 3 times.
selfCheck.aZh: 进气量减少同时哮鸣音消失，是重度梗阻加呼吸肌力竭，不是好转——按濒临呼吸骤停处理。BC 肾上腺素：0.01 mg/kg IM，上限 0.5 mg，可重复至多 3 次。

selfCheck.qEn: Why is a normal blood pressure not reassuring in a pale, tachycardic child with cool, mottled extremities?
selfCheck.qZh: 一个苍白、心动过速、四肢冰凉花斑的孩子，血压却正常，为什么不能因此放心？
selfCheck.aEn: This is the classic picture of compensated shock — the child is shunting blood centrally and raising heart rate and vascular tone to hold blood pressure up. Because children compensate efficiently, hypotension only appears once compensation fails, so a normal BP does not rule out significant shock.
selfCheck.aZh: 这就是典型的代偿性休克画面——孩子正在把血流集中到核心、靠心率和血管张力顶住血压。儿童代偿能力强，只有代偿失败后才会出现低血压，所以血压正常不能排除严重休克。

selfCheck.qEn: You suspect pediatric hypoglycemia and need to correct it under BC protocol. What BGL triggers treatment, and what dextrose concentration do you actually have on the truck?
selfCheck.qZh: 怀疑儿科低血糖，按 BC 方案该怎么纠正？血糖多少触发治疗？车上实际备的是什么浓度的葡萄糖？
selfCheck.aEn: BC treats suspected hypoglycemia at BGL < 4.0 mmol/L for any age — not the textbook's lower age-specific cutoffs. Only D10W is stocked (no D25W), dosed at 10-25 g (100-250 mL of the 10% solution).
selfCheck.aZh: BC 方案对所有年龄都是 BGL < 4.0 mmol/L 触发治疗——不是教材那套更低的分龄阈值。车上只备 D10W（没有 D25W），剂量是 10-25 g（100-250 mL 的 10% 溶液）。

bcAlerts.bookEn: The chapter warns generally against prolonged suctioning because vagal stimulation can drop the heart rate.
bcAlerts.bookZh: 教材只泛泛提醒别把吸引管留在咽后太久，迷走刺激会让心率骤降。
bcAlerts.bcEn: BC fixes the numbers: suction no more than 10-15 seconds in adults, 10 seconds in a pediatric patient, 5 seconds in an infant. Answer with these caps.
bcAlerts.bcZh: BC 给了硬数字：成人一次吸引不超过 10-15 秒，儿童 10 秒，婴儿 5 秒。考试按这套上限作答。

bcAlerts.topicZh: 肌注肾上腺素单次上限
bcAlerts.bookEn: The textbook gives pediatric epinephrine as 0.01 mg/kg IM with no explicit maximum for anaphylaxis, but caps a single asthma dose at 0.3 mg.
bcAlerts.bookZh: 教材给的儿科肾上腺素是 0.01 mg/kg IM，过敏反应部分没写明确上限，但哮喘单次剂量写了上限 0.3 mg。
bcAlerts.bcEn: BC sets one number for both anaphylaxis and severe bronchospasm with impending arrest: 0.01 mg/kg IM to a maximum of 0.5 mg, may repeat up to 3 times. Use 0.5 mg as the ceiling on the exam, not 0.3 mg.
bcAlerts.bcZh: BC 对过敏和重度支气管痉挛（濒临骤停）用同一套数字：0.01 mg/kg IM，上限 0.5 mg，可重复至多 3 次。考试按 0.5 mg 封顶，不是教材哮喘那条的 0.3 mg。

bcAlerts.bookEn: The textbook doses salbutamol nebulizer by severity/size: 2.5 mg standard starting dose, 5 mg for a larger or severely distressed child.
bcAlerts.bookZh: 教材按病情轻重/体型给沙丁胺醇雾化：标准起始 2.5 mg，个头大或重症给 5 mg。
bcAlerts.bcEn: BC ties the nebulizer dose to age instead: age >1 year gets 5 mg, age <1 year gets 2.5 mg (repeat as required). MDI dosing is weight-tiered: 10-20 kg gets 5 puffs per course, >20 kg gets 10 puffs, both repeatable up to 3 times.
bcAlerts.bcZh: BC 把雾化剂量绑在年龄上：1 岁以上给 5 mg，1 岁以下给 2.5 mg（可按需重复）。MDI 按体重分级：10-20 kg 一疗程 5 喷，>20 kg 一疗程 10 喷，都可重复至多 3 次。

bcAlerts.bookEn: The textbook splits the pediatric ipratropium dose by weight: 0.25 mg nebulized (1 MDI puff) under 10 kg, 0.5 mg (2 puffs) over 10 kg.
bcAlerts.bookZh: 教材按体重分两档给异丙托溴铵：10 kg 以下 0.25 mg 雾化（1 喷 MDI），10 kg 以上 0.5 mg（2 喷）。
bcAlerts.bcEn: BC uses one flat pediatric dose regardless of weight — 250 mcg (half a nebule) nebulized or 80 mcg (4 x 20 mcg) via MDI — and explicitly excludes neonates under 30 days. Note this matches the textbook's under-10-kg tier, not the over-10-kg one.
bcAlerts.bcZh: BC 不分体重，只给一档固定儿科剂量——250 mcg（半支雾化剂）雾化或 80 mcg（20 mcg×4）MDI——并且明确排除 30 天以下新生儿。注意这档数字对应的是教材 10 kg 以下那一档，不是 10 kg 以上那档。

bcAlerts.bookEn: The textbook gives pediatric shock resuscitation as 20 mL/kg isotonic boluses, reassessing after each, noting that as much as 60 mL/kg cumulative may be needed during transport.
bcAlerts.bookZh: 教材给的儿科休克复苏方案是每次 20 mL/kg 等渗液体，每次后重新评估，并提到转运途中累计可能需要用到 60 mL/kg。
bcAlerts.bcEn: BC's hypovolemia protocol is one number for every age: 20 mL/kg to a maximum of 2 litres total, reassessing every 500 mL. For a small child this 2 L ceiling almost never binds before local protocol or reassessment would stop you anyway, but on the exam, answer with BC's fixed 2 L cap and 500 mL reassessment interval, not the textbook's 60 mL/kg figure.
bcAlerts.bcZh: BC 的低血容量方案对所有年龄用同一套数字：20 mL/kg，总量上限 2 升，每 500 mL 重新评估一次。对小孩子来说这条 2 升的上限几乎不会先触发（早就该按方案或复评停下了），但考试作答要用 BC 固定的 2 升上限和每 500 mL 复评的节奏，不是教材说的 60 mL/kg。

bcAlerts.bookEn: The textbook's diagnostic thresholds for pediatric hypoglycemia are low: under 2.2 mmol/L in a newborn, under 3.3 mmol/L in every other infant and child.
bcAlerts.bookZh: 教材给的儿科低血糖诊断阈值比较低：新生儿 <2.2 mmol/L，其他婴儿和儿童 <3.3 mmol/L。
bcAlerts.bcEn: BC's diabetic emergency protocol uses one flat, higher treatment trigger for every age: correct suspected hypoglycemia at BGL < 4.0 mmol/L. Don't wait for the textbook's lower pediatric cutoffs on a BC exam question — 4.0 mmol/L is the number that triggers treatment.
bcAlerts.bcZh: BC 的糖尿病急症方案对所有年龄用同一条更高的固定触发线：BGL < 4.0 mmol/L 就要纠正疑似低血糖。BC 考题不要套教材那套更低的儿科阈值——4.0 mmol/L 才是触发治疗的数字。

bcAlerts.bookEn: The textbook's pediatric altered-LOC protocol calls for 25% dextrose (D25W) at 2 mL/kg IV for infants and young children, reserving 10% dextrose (D10W) for neonates.
bcAlerts.bookZh: 教材的儿科意识改变方案用 25% 葡萄糖（D25W）2 mL/kg IV 治婴幼儿，新生儿才用 10% 葡萄糖（D10W）。
bcAlerts.bcEn: BC's drug list only carries D10W — there is no D25W in the BC formulary. On the exam, correct hypoglycemia at any pediatric age with D10W (10-25 g / 100-250 mL of the 10% solution), not the textbook's D25W dose.
bcAlerts.bcZh: BC 的药物清单只有 D10W，没有 D25W。考试时不管哪个儿科年龄段，纠正低血糖都用 D10W（10-25 g / 100-250 mL 的 10% 溶液），不是教材那条 D25W 剂量。

bcAlerts.bookEn: The textbook's antidote table lists six agents as available for pediatric poisonings: flumazenil, glucagon, calcium, 100% oxygen, atropine/pralidoxime, and naloxone.
bcAlerts.bookZh: 教材的解毒剂表列了六种可用于儿科中毒的药物：氟马西尼、胰高血糖素、钙剂、100% 氧、阿托品/解磷定、纳洛酮。
bcAlerts.bcEn: BC's PCP guidelines only carry three of these: glucagon (hypoglycemia, not listed there as a beta-blocker antidote but present in scope), naloxone, and oxygen. Flumazenil, calcium as an antidote, and atropine/pralidoxime for organophosphates do not appear in the BC formulary excerpted here — treat those exposures as supportive-care-and-rapid-transport calls on the exam rather than reaching for a drug BC PCPs don't carry.
bcAlerts.bcZh: BC 的 PCP 方案里只有三样在职权范围内：胰高血糖素（方案里是治低血糖用，不是作为β阻滞剂解毒剂列出，但药本身在范围内）、纳洛酮、氧气。氟马西尼、作为解毒剂使用的钙剂、治有机磷中毒的阿托品/解磷定都不在这份 BC 用药清单里——考试遇到这几类中毒，按支持治疗加尽快转运来答，别默认 BC PCP 能直接给这些药。

bcAlerts.topicEn: Burn cooling duration and IV fluid trigger
bcAlerts.topicZh: 烧伤冷却时长与静脉补液触发线
bcAlerts.bookEn: Textbook: no specific cooling time limit is given; begin IV fluid resuscitation en route once burned BSA exceeds 5%, starting at 20 mL/kg isotonic fluid.
bcAlerts.bookZh: 教材：未给出具体冷却时限；烧伤面积超过 5% BSA 即在转运途中开始补液，等张液从 20 mL/kg 起始。
bcAlerts.bcEn: BC: cool with cool (not cold) running water for a total of 15-20 minutes, inclusive of any bystander cooling and decontamination time — never exceed 15-20 minutes. The formal hypovolemia/IV-fluid protocol indication is specifically burns >20% BSA (partial and full thickness); dose 20 mL/kg to a maximum of 2 L.
bcAlerts.bcZh: BC：用冷（非冰）流动水冷却，含旁观者已做的冷却和洗消时间在内总时长不超过 15-20 分钟。正式低血容量/静脉补液协议指征是烧伤>20% BSA（部分层+全层）；剂量 20 mL/kg，上限 2 升。
bcAlerts.ref: BC Provincial Examination Guidelines — Burn Management p.28; Hypovolemia protocol p.54

bcAlerts.topicZh: 重大烧伤创伤警报判据
bcAlerts.bookEn: Textbook: larger burns, full-thickness burns, and burns of the face/neck should go to a regional burn centre — no hard percentage cutoffs are given.
bcAlerts.bookZh: 教材：大面积烧伤、全层烧伤及面颈部烧伤应送区域烧伤中心——未给出具体百分比界限。
bcAlerts.bcEn: BC: explicit anatomical/BSA cutoffs define a major-burn trauma alert — partial-thickness burns >20% BSA, full-thickness burns >10% BSA, facial or airway burns (with or without inhalation injury), third-degree burns involving the eyes/neck/hands/feet/groin, burns that fully encircle a limb, and high-voltage electrical burns.
bcAlerts.bcZh: BC：明确列出重大烧伤创伤警报的解剖/面积界限——部分层烧伤>20% BSA、全层烧伤>10% BSA、面部或气道烧伤（含或不含吸入伤）、三度烧伤累及眼/颈/手/足/腹股沟、环形肢体烧伤、高压电烧伤。
bcAlerts.ref: BC Provincial Examination Guidelines — Trauma Triage / Anatomical Findings p.7

bcAlerts.topicEn: Taping the head during pediatric spinal motion restriction
bcAlerts.topicZh: 儿科脊柱制动中头部胶带固定
bcAlerts.bookEn: Textbook: for an oversized collar, use towel rolls, and tape may be applied across the temples and forehead (never over the chin or throat) to secure the head.
bcAlerts.bookZh: 教材：领子偏大就用毛巾卷代替，胶带可以贴过颞部和前额固定头部（绝不能贴下巴或喉部）。
bcAlerts.bcEn: BC: does not permit taping across the head or forehead at all during spinal motion restriction — secure the head by other means per BC protocol.
bcAlerts.bcZh: BC：脊柱制动时完全不允许在头部/前额贴胶带固定——按 BC 协议改用其他方式固定头部。
bcAlerts.ref: 已在本文件第13节 Pediatric Trauma 要点中标注，此处正式收录为 bcAlert

bcAlerts.topicEn: CPAP contraindications relevant to pediatric/special-needs patients
bcAlerts.topicZh: 与儿科/特殊需求患者相关的 CPAP 禁忌证
bcAlerts.bookEn: Textbook pediatric chapter: does not directly address CPAP use or contraindications for children.
bcAlerts.bookZh: 教材儿科章节：未直接讨论儿童 CPAP 使用或禁忌证。
bcAlerts.bcEn: BC: CPAP is contraindicated in patients age 12 or younger, and in any patient with a tracheostomy — both facts land directly on the special-needs population covered in Section 15.
bcAlerts.bcZh: BC：CPAP 禁用于 12 岁及以下患者，以及任何气管切开患者——这两条正好对应第15节特殊健康需求人群。
bcAlerts.ref: BC Provincial Examination Guidelines — CPAP protocol contraindications list
